name: judaism
began: c. 1000-500 bce, in the land of israel; by tradition with abraham
founder: abraham, by tradition; moses, who received the torah
scriptures: the hebrew bible (tanakh), above all the torah; the talmud
places: jerusalem, above all the western wall of the temple mount
summary: the religion of the jewish people: one god, who made a covenant with abraham and gave the torah to moses at sinai. it is the oldest of the three abrahamic faiths, and the root of christianity and islam.
creation: god created the heavens and the earth in six days and rested on the seventh, as told in the book of genesis.
age: the jewish calendar counts years from creation, which rabbinic tradition places in 3761 bce. many jews today read the six days as a teaching, not a clock, and accept the scientific age.

events.text: god creates the heavens and the earth in six days and rests on the seventh, the first sabbath. the jewish calendar counts its years from here
god forms adam from the dust of the earth and makes eve; they live in the garden of eden until they eat the forbidden fruit and are sent out
a great flood covers the earth. noah, his family, and the animals survive in the ark, and god promises never to destroy the world by flood again
people build a tower at babel to reach the heavens; god confuses their language and scatters them across the earth
abraham is born. god later calls him to leave his homeland for canaan and makes a covenant with him: his descendants will be a great nation
isaac, then jacob, who is renamed israel. jacob's twelve sons become the twelve tribes; one of them, joseph, is sold into egypt and rises to power there
moses leads the israelites out of slavery in egypt: the exodus, remembered every year at passover
at mount sinai god gives the torah to moses, including the ten commandments, and makes a covenant with the whole people

events.when: after forty years in the desert
events.text: joshua leads the israelites into the promised land of canaan
a victory stone of the pharaoh merneptah names a people called israel in canaan, the oldest mention of israel outside the bible
king david makes jerusalem his capital; his son solomon builds the first temple there
an aramean inscription found at tel dan mentions the "house of david", the oldest reference to david outside the bible
assyria destroys the northern kingdom of israel; its ten tribes are scattered and later remembered as the lost tribes
babylon destroys jerusalem and the first temple and carries many judeans into exile (rabbinic tradition dates this to 423 bce)
cyrus the great lets the exiles go home; the second temple is finished around 516 bce
under ezra and nehemiah the torah is read out in public in jerusalem; many scholars think it reached its final form around this time
the maccabees revolt against the greek seleucid kings and rededicate the temple, remembered at hanukkah
the romans destroy the second temple. judaism survives through rabbis, synagogues, prayer, and study
the bar kokhba revolt against rome is crushed; jews are banned from jerusalem and most now live in the diaspora
rabbi judah ha-nasi gathers the oral law into the mishnah
the babylonian talmud, a huge record of rabbinic debate built around the mishnah, is largely complete
rashi, in france, writes commentaries on the bible and talmud that are still printed beside the text today
maimonides, living in cairo, completes the guide for the perplexed, joining jewish faith with aristotle's philosophy
england expels its jews; france and many german states do the same over the next two centuries
spain expels its jews; many find refuge in the ottoman empire, north africa, and the netherlands
the baal shem tov begins the hasidic movement in eastern europe, stressing joy, prayer, and closeness to god
moses mendelssohn publishes jerusalem and a german translation of the torah, leading the jewish enlightenment
pogroms in the russian empire drive about two million jews to emigrate, most to the united states
theodor herzl holds the first zionist congress in basel, calling for a jewish homeland
the holocaust: nazi germany murders six million jews, about a third of all the jews in the world
the state of israel is founded
tradition looks forward to the messiah, a descendant of david, who will bring peace, gather the exiles, and rebuild the temple

people.name: adam
people.about: formed by god from the dust of the earth and placed in the garden of eden

people.name: eve
people.about: "the mother of all living", who ate the forbidden fruit with adam

people.name: noah
people.about: a righteous man saved with his family from the flood; god made a covenant with him and all living things

people.name: abraham
people.about: left his homeland at god's call; the covenant with him is the beginning of the jewish people

people.name: sarah
people.about: gave birth to isaac in old age, as god had promised

people.name: jacob
people.role: the third patriarch, also called israel
people.about: wrestled with an angel and was renamed israel; his twelve sons became the twelve tribes

people.name: joseph
people.about: sold into slavery by his brothers, he rose to rule egypt under pharaoh and saved his family from famine

people.name: moses
people.role: prophet, lawgiver, and leader of the exodus
people.about: led the israelites out of egypt and received the torah at sinai; the greatest of the prophets

people.name: miriam
people.about: led the women in song after the crossing of the sea

people.name: david
people.dates: c. 1040-970 bce, by the biblical account
people.about: shepherd, poet of the psalms, and king who made jerusalem his capital; the messiah is to be his descendant

people.name: solomon
people.dates: reigned c. 970-931 bce, by the biblical account
people.about: famous for his wisdom; built the first temple in jerusalem

people.name: elijah
people.dates: 9th century bce, by the biblical account
people.about: challenged the worship of baal and was carried to heaven in a chariot of fire; a cup is poured for him at passover

people.name: esther
people.dates: 5th century bce, by the biblical account
people.about: saved the jews of persia from destruction, remembered at the festival of purim

people.name: hillel
people.about: summed up the torah as "what is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbor; the rest is commentary"

people.name: rabbi akiva
people.about: one of the great founders of rabbinic judaism, put to death by the romans after the bar kokhba revolt

people.name: judah ha-nasi
people.role: patriarch of the jews in roman palestine
people.about: compiled the mishnah, the first written collection of the oral law

people.name: rashi
people.about: wrote the most widely read commentaries on the bible and talmud

people.name: maimonides
people.about: wrote the mishneh torah and the guide for the perplexed; "from moses to moses there was none like moses"

people.name: baal shem tov
people.about: taught that god can be served with joy in every part of life, not only through study

people.name: moses mendelssohn
people.about: led the haskalah, the jewish enlightenment, and argued for religious freedom

people.name: theodor herzl
people.role: journalist and founder of political zionism
people.about: wrote the jewish state and called the first zionist congress

people.name: anne frank
people.about: hid from the nazis in amsterdam and died in bergen-belsen; her diary is read around the world

glossary.definition: the coming of age of a jewish boy at thirteen, when he becomes responsible for keeping the commandments. for girls it is the bat mitzvah, at twelve or thirteen.
a binding agreement between god and people: with noah, with abraham, and with all israel at sinai.
the jewish communities living outside the land of israel, since the babylonian exile and above all since 70 ce.
the eight-day festival of lights, remembering the rededication of the temple by the maccabees in 164 bce.
a movement begun by the baal shem tov in the 1700s, stressing joyful prayer and devotion, led by rebbes.
food allowed by jewish law: certain animals only, slaughtered in a set way, with meat and milk kept apart.
"the anointed one": a future king descended from david who, jews believe, will bring an age of peace.
the first written collection of the oral law, compiled around 200 ce.
the spring festival remembering the exodus from egypt, with a special meal called the seder.
"my teacher": a scholar of jewish law who teaches and leads a community.
shabbat: the day of rest from friday evening to saturday evening, remembering that god rested on the seventh day.
a jewish house of prayer, study, and gathering.
the vast collection of rabbinic discussion of the mishnah, the foundation of jewish law.
the hebrew bible: the torah (teaching), the nevi'im (prophets), and the ketuvim (writings).
the five books of moses, from genesis to deuteronomy; in a wider sense, all jewish teaching.
the day of atonement, the holiest day of the year, spent in fasting and prayer.
the movement for a jewish homeland in the land of israel, which led to the founding of the state of israel in 1948.
